summary: The session ended almost exactly where it began, and that flatness is the story. The composite risk score closed at 43.09, still caution inside a goldilocks regime, up a marginal 0.36 on the day. Underneath, capital rotated violently out of AI hardware and into software: cybersecurity led at 3.1477 points and cloud computing at 3.1184 points, while networking fell 2.1924 points and memory 1.6013 points; Nvidia lost 2.179 points on the very day it headlined the largest AI infrastructure financing story on the tape. Macro remains the heaviest block at 65.33 — the real rate at 2.43 sits in the 99.04 percentile and the nominal ten year yield at 4.69 in the 97.99 percentile, both repriced higher today. The contradiction that matters is that volatility slept through it: the VIX eased to 14.9 and realized volatility printed 14.0039; credit refused to blink either, with high yield at 2.7 and investment grade at 0.78.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Macro is the heaviest dimension at 65.33 and it got heavier today: the ten year real rate rose to 2.43, a 99.04 percentile reading, while the nominal ten year yield at 4.69 and the two year at 4.25 both repriced higher from 4.63 and 4.18.
Cross-asset confirmation at 0.625 is the single largest contributor to the composite, adding 7.5 points, and it is the one block where the signal is genuinely mixed rather than benign.

AI hardware de-rated on its own good news: Nvidia fell 2.179 points, semiconductor equipment 1.4402 points, memory 1.6013 points and networking 2.1924 points — on the same day the tape was digesting a record private financing package for AI infrastructure.

Hawkish Fed commentary landed on top of a contracting payroll print: the session's highest ranked macro headline scored 59.71 on importance and argued for further hikes, while payrolls printed -23.0 against an effective funds rate still at 3.63.
Leadership is narrow: only 0.1032 of the tape made new highs while 0.671 sits above its two hundred day average, so the advance is being carried by a thin cohort.

supporting_signals.claim: Semis relative strength is negative at -1.5511, confirming that the hardware complex is lagging rather than leading.
Crypto de-risked across the board, with Bitcoin at 63937.0, Ether at 1876.08 and Solana at 75.98, all lower on the day.
The dollar index held firm at 119.7034 while the real rate sat at 2.43, a combination that tightens financial conditions without any help from credit spreads.

contradicting_signals.claim: Credit is not confirming any stress: high yield OAS at 2.7 and investment grade at 0.78 both remain deep in the calm end of their range.
Volatility stayed suppressed, with the VIX at 14.9 and realized volatility at 14.0039.
The trend structure is still intact: price sits 9.8853 above its two hundred day average, the drawdown from the fifty two week high is only -0.031, and three month momentum is 4.7992.
Software leadership was broad rather than a single name: cybersecurity 3.1477, cloud computing 3.1184, enterprise software 2.2203 and AI software 2.1718 all advanced together.
New lows remain negligible at 0.0129, so the rotation is not yet spilling into broad distribution.

what_changed_today: The composite risk score rose 0.36 to 43.09, extending a 0.62 gain over the week.
Rates repriced higher across the curve: the ten year moved from 4.63 to 4.69, the two year from 4.18 to 4.25 and the real rate from 2.41 to 2.43.
Leadership flipped inside technology, with cybersecurity up 3.1477 and cloud up 3.1184 while networking fell 2.1924 and memory fell 1.6013.
The VIX eased from 15.15 to 14.9 even as rates and energy moved against risk.
Overnight reverse repo balances collapsed from 1.45 to 0.975, a liquidity plumbing move that now scores 88.92 on risk.
Nvidia closed at 219.080002, down 2.179, despite headlining the day's biggest AI capital story.
watch_next: Wednesday's CPI print is the week's binary event; prediction markets lean toward a tamer number, which is the setup most exposed to an upside surprise.
Whether the ten year holds above 4.69 or backs off decides if the macro block keeps its 65.33 weight in the composite.
Watch whether the software bid persists or fades: a one day 3.1477 move in cybersecurity is as likely to be a conference echo as the start of a durable rotation.
Producer prices on Thursday and retail sales on Friday complete the inflation and demand picture before the next Fed window.
Cisco reports Wednesday and is the first read on whether networking weakness is a price move or an earnings problem.
Energy and Strait of Hormuz headlines remain the fastest route from a calm tape to a repriced one.

bull_case.title: Disinflation confirms and the rotation broadens
points: A soft CPI would pull the real rate back from 2.43 and relieve the 99.04 percentile pressure that is currently the single biggest macro drag.
Credit is already voting for this outcome, with high yield at 2.7 in the 8.79 percentile.
If software leadership holds, the 0.671 breadth reading can improve without semiconductors having to lead.

base_case.title: Caution holds, rotation continues, no regime change
points: The composite stays near 43.09 with the regime still goldilocks, because low volatility at 14.9 and tight credit at 2.7 offset the macro block.
Capital keeps rotating within technology rather than leaving it, leaving the index flat while dispersion stays high.
Cross-asset confirmation stays around 0.625, neither confirming a breakdown nor clearing the risk.

bear_case.title: A hot CPI meets a market priced for calm
points: With the VIX at 14.9 and realized volatility at 14.0039, there is no cushion priced for an inflation surprise.
A push in the ten year above 4.69 with the real rate above 2.43 would hit the same long duration equity complex that just fell 2.1924 in networking and 1.6013 in memory.
Narrow leadership at 0.1032 new highs means the index has little to fall back on if the software bid fails.
